parameters.content:
## AI blog posts with images, formatted for WPBakery

Most AI-to-WordPress workflows push plain HTML, which lands in a page-builder
theme as one undifferentiated block you then rebuild by hand. This one formats
the body as **WPBakery** shortcodes, so the post opens in the visual editor
already laid out.

Produces: article body, excerpt, FAQ, SEO metadata and a header image.

### Setup
1. Open **Test Data** and paste your API keys into `ai_config`.
2. Enable at least one text provider and one image provider.
3. Run **Test Trigger** to try the whole thing end to end.
4. For real use, POST the same payload shape to the **Webhook**.

No credentials are stored in this workflow. Keys travel in the request body, so
the caller (a WordPress plugin, or anything else) supplies its own.

### Two ways in

**Webhook** — production. POST your topic plus `ai_config`.

**Test Trigger → Test Data** — the same payload hardcoded, so you can run and
debug without a caller. Edit the sample inside **Test Data**.

### Normalize

Merges the incoming body with any `existing_data`, applies defaults for tone,
image style and categories, and lifts `ai_config` out of the payload.

Everything downstream reads this one shape, so defaults live here rather than
being repeated in each node.

### Routing

**Mode Switch** — `mode: "regenerate"` goes to the regeneration branches.
Anything else runs the full pipeline.

**Action Switch** — sends a regeneration request to the right branch:
`image`, `excerpt`, `faq` or `seo`.

### Full generation

**Metadata** — category, excerpt, FAQ and SEO fields from the source text.
**Rewrite** — the article body, wrapped in WPBakery shortcodes.
**Image + Output** — writes an image prompt, generates the image, assembles the
final response.

### Regenerate one piece at a time

An AI draft is rarely wrong all over. If the excerpt reads flat or the image
missed the brief, re-run just that part instead of the whole post. Each branch
answers on its own webhook response, so the caller can offer a
"try that bit again" button.

### Provider fallbacks

Every AI call walks a provider list in order — Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek,
OpenRouter for text; Gemini then OpenAI for images. Providers you leave
unconfigured are skipped.

Rate limits and 5xx responses retry with a delay (`retry_count`, `retry_delay`)
before falling through to the next provider. A provider outage costs you a
slower run rather than a failed one.
